---
title: "Web vinext Workers"
description: "apps/web built with vinext on Vite+ as route-family Cloudflare Workers: families, build, checks, bindings and known gaps."
updatedAt: "2026-11-26"
audience: developers
---

`apps/web` also builds with [vinext](https://github.com/cloudflare/vinext),
a Vite+ implementation of the Next.js API, into route-free Cloudflare Workers
named `tuturuuu-web-vinext-<family>`. The gateway reaches them through service
bindings (see [Gateway Worker](/build/devops/gateway-worker)). The Next.js
build is unchanged: `next.config.ts` and `vite.vinext.config.ts` both build
their config from `next-config.web.ts`, and `next.config.test.ts` checks that
the two agree.

## Why families

The whole app is 17.3 MiB gzip as one Worker (`cf deploy --dry-run`), over the
10 MiB upload limit. `apps/web/cloudflare/vinext/families.json` splits it:

| Family | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `api-core` | `/api/**` except the OpenNext global deny list |
| `api-ops` | The OpenNext global deny list (crons, devboxes, infrastructure, account switching, immediate notifications) |
| `public-auth` | `[locale]` sign-in and auth pages, the landing page and marketing pages outside the public docs family |
| `dashboard` | `[locale]/[wsId]/**` except the `dashboard-apps` paths |
| `dashboard-apps` | `[locale]/[wsId]/{tasks,whiteboards,mind,documents,calendar,habits,notes,inventory,epm}` and their subtrees |
| `web-rest` | Every other route entry |

`nodeOnly` lists entries that still need Node-only APIs, which no family
owns. It is empty. `families.test.ts` checks that every route entry has exactly
one family and that only `api-ops` owns denied paths.

The gateway passes `x-tuturuuu-mobile-client` and `x-tuturuuu-turnstile-token`
to Web family bindings on API mutations. Web verifies the session binding or
Turnstile proof before handling the request. The gateway still strips other
client-supplied forwarding headers. The Mira dispatch case in
`apps/gateway/src/web-route-table.test.ts` covers this boundary.

## Building a family

Builds run in a disposable checkout, because they delete unowned routes and
upgrade React to 19.3.1, which vinext requires. The monorepo keeps its React
pin.

`build-family.sh` refuses to run when:

- the checkout has no disposable marker;
- Node is older than 24.22, which cannot strip TypeScript (use the version in
  `.node-version`);
- the checkout sits under another directory with a `tsconfig.json`, such as
  `.worktrees/` in the main checkout. Vite+ resolves `tsconfig.json` upward
  past the checkout root, so create the checkout elsewhere, for example
  `~/.t3/scratch/vinext-<family>`.

```bash
git worktree add --detach ~/.t3/scratch/vinext-<family> <sha>
cd ~/.t3/scratch/vinext-<family> && bun install
printf 'disposable checkout for an OpenNext family build\n' > apps/web/.opennext-disposable-checkout
set -a; . <build-env-file>; set +a   # NEXT_PUBLIC_* values, inlined at build time
export NEXT_PUBLIC_TUTURUUU_ACTIVE_APP_MOUNTS=infra
PLATFORM_BUILD_ENVIRONMENT=production PLATFORM_BUILD_REF_NAME=main \
  PLATFORM_BUILD_COMMIT_HASH=<sha> bun run --silent scripts/ci/generate-build-metadata.ts
bash apps/web/cloudflare/vinext/build-family.sh <family>
```

The build-env file holds `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_DISCORD_LINK` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SHORTENER_URL`. The metadata step
stamps `/api/build-info` with the commit, so build every family from a commit
on `main`.

`build-family.sh` builds the workspace packages, prunes with
`cloudflare/vinext/prune.ts`, runs `vp build --config vite.vinext.config.ts`,
runs `cf deploy --dry-run --prebuilt`, then
`scripts/ci/web-vinext-bundle-check.mjs`. The check fails when the resolved
`react-server-dom-webpack` is vulnerable to GHSA-xqc2-xf4c-x3h3 (below
19.2.9, 19.3.0 or any prerelease), when any emitted module carries the real
Redis client, or when the upload exceeds the 9.5 MiB family budget.
`build-family.sh` also runs the version check right after install. The result,
including the resolved version, is in
`apps/web/cloudflare/vinext/<family>.check.json`.

Before `vp build`, `build-family.sh` runs `cloudflare/vinext/service-worker.ts`.
The Next.js route `src/app/serwist/[path]/route.ts` bundles `src/app/sw.ts`
with esbuild-wasm and reads the revision through `node:child_process` at
prerender time. Neither runs in a Worker. For the family that keeps that route
(`web-rest`), the helper calls `buildOfflineWorker` from `@tuturuuu/offline/route`
with the same config (`src/lib/offline-worker-config.ts`): the offline
fallback `/~offline`, no public-file precache, and the checkout's commit as
revision. It then replaces the route with `createPrebuiltOfflineRoute`
(`@tuturuuu/offline/route/prebuilt`). `/serwist/sw.js` and `/serwist/sw.js.map`
are served from the prebuilt bytes with the Next.js headers
(`application/javascript`, `Service-Worker-Allowed: /`). A family build has no
`.next/static`, so its precache manifest holds only the offline fallback.
Hashed assets are cached when first fetched.

`build-family.sh` also exports `PLATFORM_DEPLOYMENT_STAMP` as the first 12
characters of the build commit. `cloudflare.config.ts` binds it as a text var,
so the `/serwist/sw.js?v=<stamp>` cache-buster in `src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx`
changes with each build. `cloudflare/vinext/service-worker.test.ts` checks the
single owner, the order of the build steps, the binding and the parity with the
Next.js route.

Every family response, including 404s, redirects and 401/403/405 API answers,
carries `x-tuturuuu-build: <full 40-hex commit>`; staged 0% smokes
(`Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Overrides`) read it as the signed-out version
identity. `build-family.sh` exports `PLATFORM_BUILD_COMMIT`, and
`cloudflare/vinext/build-stamp-plugin.ts` bakes it into the Worker entry
wrapper and the client `_headers`. The wrapper overwrites any upstream value
and omits the header when the build has no commit. A thrown error is logged
scrubbed and re-thrown, so it still surfaces as a Worker exception and a
gateway 502, without the header. `build-stamp.test.ts` covers the contract.

Assets served without the Worker (`/_next/static/*`, `/_f/<id>/_next/static/*`)
are stamped only through `_headers`, which takes effect only when the uploader
sends the file's contents as the assets config: in the Workers script or
version upload metadata, `"assets": { "jwt": "<completion jwt>", "config": {
"_headers": "<contents of the client _headers>", ... } }`, and leaves
`_headers` out of the uploaded asset manifest. A plain upload serves it as the
public file `/_headers` and stamps no asset (the cf Build Output rehearsal in
`scripts/ci/fixtures/cf-toolchain-receipts.json` records that `_headers` ships
as a plain asset there, so verify `cf deploy --prebuilt` too). With
`PLATFORM_BUILD_COMMIT` set, `web-vinext-bundle-check.mjs` fails unless the
client output holds a `/*` rule with the stamp; uploaders can run
`node scripts/ci/web-vinext-bundle-check.mjs --stamp <client-dir> <commit>`
first. The smoke then expects `x-tuturuuu-build` on a
`/_f/<family>/_next/static/*` asset and a 404 for `/_f/<family>/_headers`.

Worker builds emit no source maps (`build.sourcemap: false`): Cloudflare
rejects an upload whose source maps exceed 60 MiB (error 10021), and the
`public-auth` maps alone reach about 70 MiB.

## CI sealed builds

`.github/workflows/web-vinext-families-build.yaml` builds and seals families
in GitHub Actions instead of on an operator machine. It runs on
`workflow_dispatch` only, with inputs `sha` (an exact 40-hex commit) and
`families` (a comma list; empty builds every enabled family in
`families.json`). It never publishes: the token is `contents: read`, it reads
no secret and holds no Cloudflare credential. The `cf deploy --dry-run` inside
`build-family.sh` runs locally without credentials.

The workflow:

1. Runs only for `tutur3u/platform` dispatched from `main`. It refuses a `sha`
   that is not 40 lowercase hex or not an ancestor of `origin/main` or
   `origin/production`, and checks that `HEAD` is that commit.
2. Builds each family in its own job (Node from `.node-version`, Bun 1.4.4,
   frozen install, no caches, extra swap). It generates the build metadata
   with `PLATFORM_BUILD_ENVIRONMENT=production` and runs `build-family.sh`.
3. Seals the build with `scripts/ci/web-vinext-seal.mjs seal`, re-verifies it
   with `scripts/ci/web-vinext-sealed-artifact.mjs`, and uploads the artifact
   `web-vinext-sealed-<family>`.
4. Downloads every family artifact in a fresh job, verifies each one again and
   uploads `web-vinext-sealed-receipt` (`receipt.json`). The receipt job runs
   only when every family succeeded, so a run without a receipt is not
   publishable even if some family artifacts exist. Artifacts are kept 7 days.
5. Signs a build provenance attestation for every artifact zip in the
   `attest` job. It is the only job with `id-token: write` and
   `attestations: write`, it checks out nothing, and it reads the zip digests
   from GitHub's artifact API. The jobs that run code from the pin hold
   `contents: read` only, so their runners never get an OIDC token.

The run title is `Web vinext families <sha>`, which ties a run to its pin.

### Build environment

The `build` jobs use the GitHub environment `web-vinext-build`. Create it,
with deployment branches restricted to exactly `main` (custom branch
policies), before the first dispatch. A job that names a missing environment
makes GitHub create it unprotected, and `vars.*` then falls back to
repository and organization variables. The provenance check refuses a run
when the environment is missing or open to another branch, and the env guard
fails the build when any of the eight values is empty. The environment holds
eight **variables** and no secrets:

| Variable | Sensitivity |
| --- | --- |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` | Public |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL` | Public |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | Public |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Public (the publishable key, never `sb_secret_`) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` | Public (site key, not the Turnstile secret) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID` | Public |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISCORD_LINK` | Public |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SHORTENER_URL` | Public |

All eight are inlined into both the client and the server bundles, so they are
readable in every artifact and in the served pages. No real secret is needed
at build time: `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` and
`ABUSE_GUARD_KEY_PEPPER` are Worker secrets bound at upload
(`cloudflare.config.ts` declares names only). `build-family.sh` derives
`NEXT_PUBLIC_TUTURUUU_ACTIVE_APP_MOUNTS`, `PLATFORM_BUILD_COMMIT` and
`PLATFORM_DEPLOYMENT_STAMP` from the checkout. `CALENDAR_APP_URL` and
`NEXT_PUBLIC_CALENDAR_APP_URL` are optional and unset, as in operator builds.

Because a public repository's artifacts are downloadable by anyone with read
access, two guards keep secrets out of them:

- `web-vinext-seal.mjs env-guard` runs before the install. It fails, naming
  variables only, when a public value is empty, when another `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`
  name is present (it would be inlined), when a `CLOUDFLARE_*`/`CF_*` name is
  present, when any other secret-looking name (`*TOKEN*`, `*SECRET*`,
  `*_KEY`, `*PASSWORD*`, `*PEPPER*`) is set, or when a public value has a
  secret shape.
- The seal scans every sealed file before writing `seal.json`. It refuses the
  value of any secret-looking variable in the job environment (at least 8
  characters), Supabase secret keys, service-role JWTs, PEM private keys,
  GitHub tokens, Stripe live keys, AWS access key ids, OpenAI and Anthropic
  API keys, and `.env*`, `.dev.vars*` or `secrets.json` files. Findings
  name the file and the variable or rule, never the value.

### Sealed layout

Download into one directory per family, then the receipt:

```bash
gh run download <run-id> -R tutur3u/platform -n web-vinext-sealed-<family> -D sealed/<family>
gh run download <run-id> -R tutur3u/platform -n web-vinext-sealed-receipt -D sealed
```

```text
sealed/
  receipt.json            schema, sha, families.<id>.{worker, sealSha256, moduleCount, fileCount}
  <family>/
    seal.json             see below
    output/               apps/web/.cloudflare/output of the build, unchanged
      v1/workers/default/bundle/index.mjs   main module
    client/               only when the build put client assets in dist/client
    assets-manifest.json  assetsDir, headersFile, files.<path>.{sha256, bytes}
    check.json            web-vinext-bundle-check.mjs result (Redis, RSDW, size, stamp)
    dry-run.log           cf deploy --dry-run --prebuilt output
    imports-check.json    mainModule, moduleCount, closure: "ok", stampModules
```

`seal.json` (`schema: tuturuuu.web-vinext-seal/v1`) holds `family`,
`worker` (`tuturuuu-web-vinext-<family>`), `sha`, `deploymentStamp` (first 12
characters), `bundleDir` (`output/v1/workers/default/bundle`), `mainModule`
(`index.mjs`, relative to `bundleDir`), `assetsDir`, `stampModule` (a module
containing both `x-tuturuuu-build` and the quoted sha), `moduleCount`,
`modules` (bundle-relative path to sha256, sorted), `fileCount`, `files`
(sealed-directory path to `{sha256, bytes}` for every file except
`seal.json`, sorted) and `build` (repository, run id, attempt, workflow ref).
Modules are every `.js`/`.mjs` file under `bundleDir`, excluding `.map` files
and dot directories.

Send `<assetsDir>/_headers` as the assets config `_headers`, never as an
uploaded asset (see the stamp notes above).

### Verifying before publishing

The sealed verifier proves only that an artifact is internally consistent,
not where it came from. A copy of the workflow dispatched from another branch
can produce an artifact that passes it. Check origin first, from a checkout
of `main`, with a `gh` signed in to an account that can read the repository's
environments:

```bash
node scripts/ci/web-vinext-sealed-provenance.mjs <run-id> <sha> <empty-out-dir>
```

It refuses (exit 10) a run that is not
`.github/workflows/web-vinext-families-build.yaml` on `tutur3u/platform`,
dispatched with `workflow_dispatch` from `main` and successful, or whose
workflow commit is not on `main`. It refuses (11) a run title that does not
name the sha, a sha on neither `main` nor `production`, and any seal or
receipt whose `build`/`run` names another run or workflow ref. It downloads
every `web-vinext-sealed-*` zip and refuses (12) a missing, extra or expired
artifact or a zip whose sha256 differs from GitHub's digest. It runs
`gh attestation verify --signer-workflow
tutur3u/platform/.github/workflows/web-vinext-families-build.yaml
--source-ref refs/heads/main --source-digest <workflow commit>
--deny-self-hosted-runners` on each zip and refuses (13) a missing attestation
or one from another run. It refuses (14) a `web-vinext-build` environment
that is missing or allows a branch other than `main`. Only then does it
extract `<out>/sealed/<family>` and `<out>/sealed/receipt.json` and run the
sealed receipt verifier, whose exit codes follow. Publish from that `sealed/`
directory only.

The sealed verifier can also run on its own:

```bash
node scripts/ci/web-vinext-sealed-artifact.mjs --receipt sealed/receipt.json sealed <sha>
node scripts/ci/web-vinext-sealed-artifact.mjs sealed/<family> <sha> --family <family>
```

It re-hashes every file, refuses extra files and symlinks, requires the
fixed layout (`bundleDir`, `mainModule` `index.mjs`, `assetsDir` one of
`output/v1/workers/default/assets` or `client`), compares the module set and
count, checks every assets manifest entry, the `_headers` stamp, the stamp
module, the module closure and the secret scan.

| Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Verified |
| 2 | Usage error, or `seal.json`/`receipt.json` missing or unreadable |
| 3 | Pin mismatch: wrong or malformed sha, family, worker, stamp or schema |
| 4 | Tamper: hash, size, file set, module count or receipt digest differs, or a symlink |
| 5 | Missing: a sealed file, module, main module, assets directory or family |
| 6 | Stamp: no `_headers` rule, or no module with the header and quoted sha |
| 7 | Closure: a module imports an unsealed module |
| 8 | Secret: a secret-shaped value or forbidden file name |
| 10 | Provenance: run repository, workflow path, event, branch or result |
| 11 | Provenance: run title, sha off `main`/`production`, or a seal bound to another run |
| 12 | Provenance: artifact missing, extra, expired or digest mismatch |
| 13 | Provenance: attestation missing or from another signer, ref, commit or run |
| 14 | Provenance: `web-vinext-build` missing or not restricted to `main` |

Tests: `scripts/ci/web-vinext-seal.test.mjs` (seal, tamper, missing module,
wrong sha, decoy layout, manifest entries, symlinks, secret refusal, env
guard), `scripts/ci/web-vinext-sealed-provenance.test.mjs` (wrong branch,
workflow, event, sha, digest, attestation and environment) and
`scripts/ci/web-vinext-families-build-workflow.test.mjs` (dispatch only,
`contents: read` for pin-code jobs, signing only in `attest`, no secrets or
Cloudflare credential, pinned actions).

## Deploying a family

A new Worker needs its secrets in the first upload. From `apps/web` of the
built checkout:

```bash
CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=... WEB_VINEXT_FAMILY=<family> node_modules/.bin/cf deploy \
  --prebuilt --no-provision --secrets-file <secrets.json> --message "vinext <family> <full-sha>"
```

The production deployment proof reads each family's `PLATFORM_DEPLOYMENT_STAMP`
binding (the first 12 characters of the build commit, set by
`build-family.sh`), so build every family from one main commit. Use the full
40-character commit in the message so the serving version names its source.

A redeploy of an existing Worker omits `--secrets-file`; its secrets carry
over. The deploy reports `No targets deployed`: the Worker has no routes,
custom domains, workers.dev or preview URLs. A family the gateway flags takes
production traffic as soon as the deploy finishes, so:

1. Before deploying, record the version that serves the Worker now
   (`GET /accounts/<account>/workers/scripts/tuturuuu-web-vinext-<family>/deployments`,
   the first deployment's version at 100%). That is the rollback target.
2. Deploy, then confirm the new version is at 100% in the same listing. The
   listing can show 100% a few seconds before the edge serves the new
   version, so the smoke in the next step retries `/api/build-info` for up to
   40 seconds before treating an old commit as a failure.
3. Smoke through `https://tuturuuu.com`: every response carries
   `x-gateway-family: <family>`. Check `/api/build-info` (api-core) for the
   commit and `environment: production`, a page of the family (for example
   `/vi/login` for public-auth) and one `/_f/<family>/_next/static/*` asset it
   references.
4. On any failure, roll back at once: create a deployment of the recorded
   version at 100% (`POST .../deployments` with
   `{"strategy":"percentage","versions":[{"version_id":"<previous>","percentage":100}]}`).

### Manual version-only publication: verified API behavior

When families are published with an operator-run, version-only driver
(upload a version, verify it, then deploy it at 100%) instead of `cf deploy`,
these Cloudflare API behaviors apply. A driver that assumes otherwise stops
fail-closed (traffic unchanged), so handle each one before the write window.

- **Asset upload buckets.** `POST /accounts/<account>/workers/assets/upload`
  answers `202 Accepted` for every non-final bucket and `201` with
  `result.jwt` only for the final one. Accept 200, 201 and 202 with
  `success: true`, and take the completion JWT from the final non-empty
  bucket only.
- **Secret inheritance.** `{"type":"inherit","name":N,"version_id":V}` is
  rejected (HTTP 400, code 10057 once per secret). Only name-only
  `{"type":"inherit","name":N}` is accepted, and it copies values from the
  Worker's **latest** version. Require latest == serving before the upload
  (and again immediately before the version POST) so secrets come from the
  version serving traffic.
- **Module readback.** `GET .../workers/scripts/<worker>/versions/<id>?include=modules`
  returns no `modules` or `main_module`. Two sources do return bytes:
  - `GET .../workers/scripts/<worker>/content/v2` (multipart/form-data, one
    part per module, `cf-entrypoint: index.mjs`). It **ignores `?version=`**
    and returns the latest version, so bracket the read with
    latest == the new version immediately before and after it.
  - `GET .../workers/workers/<worker>/versions/<id>?include=modules` (the
    Workers API path) returns `modules[].content_base64`, `main_module`,
    `migration_tag` and bindings. Cron Control's CI verifier
    (`apps/cron-control/scripts/verify-already-serving.mjs`) and any serving
    proof generator must use this path.
- **Leftover versions.** A run that stops after the version POST leaves a 0%
  version that becomes latest, so the latest == serving fence refuses later
  runs. Record it, and let the release authority accept that exact version id
  by name for the next run (its secrets were inherited while latest == serving).

### Partial round recovery

Publishing several families in one run can stop after earlier families are
already at 100%. The driver must then print a rollback command for every
family it already deployed, newest first, in addition to the stopped family's
own outcome. Operator procedure:

1. Halt; do not re-run the publish. Keep stdout, stderr, the preimage and the
   run ledger.
2. Read live state for all families (deployments and latest version) against
   the preimage. A ledger `deploy-start` without `deployed` means that deploy
   is uncertain: trust only the live readback.
3. With the release authority, roll forward the rest (new packet and ACK) or
   roll back every family whose live version differs from its preimage
   serving version, newest first. Use `curl --fail-with-body`, confirm
   `success: true`, then re-read every family at 100%.

### Operator host notes

- Keep the driver directory and its `state/` run directory at mode `0700`.
  A recursive `chmod 600 <dir>/*` strips the directory execute bit, and the
  publish then refuses before any write because it cannot create its run
  directory.
- `gh` cannot read the macOS keychain over a non-interactive SSH session. Do
  not copy GitHub tokens between machines: download a producer artifact on a
  host where `gh` is signed in and have the proof tool verify it against
  GitHub's published artifact digest.
- Non-interactive SSH has a minimal `PATH`; add the directories that hold
  `node` (`/usr/local/bin` on the Macbook hosts) explicitly.

## Gateway routing

The gateway routes each family from
`apps/gateway/src/web-routes.generated.json`. Regenerate it with
`bun run --cwd apps/web routes:gateway` after changing routes or
`families.json`. See [Gateway Worker](/build/devops/gateway-worker#vinext-family-route-table)
for matching, flags, cutover and rollback. A family build sets `assetPrefix`
to `/_f/<id>` from `WEB_VINEXT_FAMILY`, so each family's client assets have
their own URL base. Page families need that build before their id goes into
`GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES`.

All six families are flagged. Web has no HTTP origin: a path no flagged
family claims, including unprefixed `/_next/static/*` and `/_f/<id>/*` for an
id no Worker builds, goes to the bound `web-rest` family, and without that
binding the gateway answers `503`.

**Rollback ladder:** a broken family Worker rolls back to its previous Worker
version (above). A broken routing change rolls back by re-assigning the
previous gateway version. Removing an id from `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` sends
that family's paths to `web-rest`, which does not own them, so it is not a
rollback.

## Runtime bindings

`apps/web/cloudflare.config.ts` declares the Worker (`workersDev` and
`previewUrls` off, no routes):

- `ABUSE_GUARD` service binding to `tuturuuu-abuse-guard`
  (`AbuseGuardEntrypoint`) for proxy, rate-limit and native-integrity state.
  `@upstash/redis` is aliased to `cloudflare/opennext/redis-unavailable.ts`.
- `IMAGES` (Cloudflare Images) behind `ImageTransformer` for profile media,
  feedback images and external project assets. Animated input is flattened
  to one frame. A profile upload makes at most six transformations.
- `CHATGPT_FILES`, the private R2 bucket `tuturuuu-web-chatgpt-files`, on
  `api-ops` and the whole-app build only. See
  [ChatGPT credential storage](#chatgpt-credential-storage).
- Secret names only for Supabase, app coordination and the abuse-guard
  pepper. `@opennextjs/cloudflare` resolves to
  `cloudflare/vinext/cloudflare-context.ts`, which reads `cloudflare:workers`.

## ChatGPT credential storage

`api-ops` serves `/api/ai/chatgpt`, `/api/ai/chatgpt/new` and
`/api/v1/users/chatgpt`. These routes back the
[ChatGPT plan](/platform/ai/chatgpt-subscriptions) picker beside the Mira chat
model picker. They list, use and disconnect a user's ChatGPT subscription
accounts. They hold per-user OAuth credential stores (access and refresh
tokens), not uploaded files. The routes answer `404` or `enabled: false`
unless `TUTURUUU_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=self-hosted` and `OPENAI_CHATGPT_ENABLED=true`.

`src/lib/chatgpt/storage.ts` picks a `ChatGPTStorageAdapter` per call:

- `storage-r2.ts` when the Worker binds `CHATGPT_FILES`. Each user has one
  object at `chatgpt/<userId>/store.json`, where `userId` is the session user's
  UUID and the object name is a constant, so no client input reaches a key.
  The object records its owner in custom metadata, and a read rejects a
  mismatch. A create-only `chatgpt/<userId>/store.lock` object
  (`If-None-Match: *`) serializes refresh-token rotation. A lock older
  than 45 seconds is taken over with an ETag-conditional write. The closing
  store write is fenced on the ETag of the opening one, so a request that
  outlived its lock fails instead of overwriting newer tokens.
- `storage-fs.ts` otherwise (local development, tests, self-hosted Node):
  owner-only files under `CHATGPT_SUBSCRIPTIONS_DIR` or
  `~/.config/tuturuuu/chatgpt`.

Both adapters share the store schema, UUID validation and the
persist-before-operation order. Tests: `storage-r2.test.ts` (fake bucket
round-trip, owner isolation, traversal, locking) and `storage.test.ts`
(filesystem).

There is nothing to migrate. The hosted service never enables the
integration. On Vercel, any credential file would have lived on the ephemeral
function filesystem, so it was never durable. Create the bucket before the
first `api-ops` deploy, with no public access and no `r2.dev` URL:

```bash
cf r2 buckets create --name tuturuuu-web-chatgpt-files
```

The hosted Workers do not set `TUTURUUU_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` or
`OPENAI_CHATGPT_ENABLED`, so they answer the disabled responses and never read
the bucket. `scripts/chatgpt-connect.ts` writes only the filesystem store, so
nothing populates the R2 store yet.

## Worker runtime behavior

- `cloudflare.config.ts` enables Workers observability (logs at a head
  sampling rate of 1, with invocation logs), so every family deploy keeps
  requests and console output queryable in Workers Logs.
- The `api-*` families, and the unsplit Worker, run with
  `placement: { region: 'aws:ap-southeast-1' }`. At the nearest edge,
  Vietnamese traffic mostly lands in Hong Kong, and the Gemini API rejects
  requests from Hong Kong as an unsupported location. Mira and AI chat then
  fail before the first token, as a generic stream error. Singapore is a
  supported region and sits beside the Supabase database. The page families
  stay at the edge.
- `cloudflare/vinext/worker-entry.ts` is the Worker entrypoint. It installs
  `cloudflare/vinext/workers-fetch.ts`, because workerd's fetch rejects every
  `cache` mode except `no-store` ("Unsupported cache mode"). The bundler
  inlines the entry's side-effect imports into the entry chunk, which runs
  after every chunk it imports, so `cloudflare/vinext/workers-fetch-first.ts`
  makes vinext's fetch-cache shim import the install module: ESM dependency
  order then runs the install before vinext captures the network fetch. vinext keeps its own handling of `cache`, `next.revalidate` and
  `next.tags`, and the network fetch drops the mode workerd rejects.
  workerd's fetch and `Request` constructor also throw `Invalid redirect
  value` for `redirect: 'error'`, which server code (the Mastermind store
  client, `@tuturuuu/internal-api`, auth attestation and asset fetches) passes
  so credentialed requests never follow a redirect. The installed global
  fetch, and any patch later assigned to it such as vinext's caching fetch,
  sends those requests with `redirect: 'manual'` and fails a 3xx response
  with a `TypeError`. Without it every such call fails, and the Mastermind
  fleet routes answer `503 {"error":"unavailable"}`.
  `bun run --cwd apps/web test:vinext:runtime` checks both in workerd, and
  that a secret no config declares reaches `process.env` as a whole object
  and by a dynamic key.
- Workers send no User-Agent on subrequests, and the proxy answers 400 to a
  sessionless API request without one. `@tuturuuu/internal-api` therefore
  sends `User-Agent: tuturuuu-<service>/1.0` on server requests that set none,
  with the service from `TUTURUUU_SERVICE_NAME`. External apps on Workers are
  exempt from that one rule only for server-to-server calls the route itself
  authenticates (`apps/web/src/lib/proxy-auth-header.ts`): a JSON `POST` to
  `/api/v1/auth/app-token/exchange`, a bearer shaped like an app-coordination
  token (`ttr_app_<header>.<claims>.<signature>`; shape only, never verified or
  trusted by the proxy), or `Authorization: Basic` on `POST` to exactly
  `/api/v1/integrations/upskii/{introspect,link-status,unlink}`. Those three
  routes are also the only place a `Basic` header is not a
  `malformed-auth-header` 401. Neither exemption is counted as abuse by the
  proxy, and rate limits, the query/scanner rules and route authentication
  still apply. Instead the Upskii routes count their own failed Basic checks
  (`lib/integrations/upskii/auth-failure.ts`), scoped to those routes. They
  never feed the global edge IP block, so a bad or rotated Upskii secret cannot
  cut a source off from other APIs.
  - Failures from an address source (IPv6 grouped by /64) count per source
    and client id. After 5 in 10 minutes the pair gets 429 on those routes,
    before the secret check, until the window ends. Sending the right secret
    recovers it after that.
  - A Worker-zone source (`cf-worker`, which is how the real Upskii server
    calls) is never locked out, because that header is not proven for every
    client egressing from Cloudflare (WARP, for example). Per-IP admission,
    pacing and the 256-bit secret bound guessing there. An `unknown` source
    (no trusted client address) is never locked out either, because every such
    caller would share one key. The first one from client id `upskii` per
    isolate logs `UPSKII_AUTH_SOURCE_UNKNOWN`.
  - Failures per client id across all sources log `UPSKII_AUTH_FAILURE_SURGE`
    past `accountLinkAuthFailure`, but never lock the client id out.
  - Every counter fails closed: without its store the routes answer 503 rather
    than allow unlimited guesses. Other
  paths, methods, trailing slashes and encoded variants keep both blocks.
  Clients should still send a User-Agent.

## Local check

After a build, `vp preview --config vite.vinext.config.ts --configLoader runner`
serves the Worker in workerd. Put disposable values in `apps/web/.dev.vars`
(gitignored). Delete it afterwards.

## Known gaps

- `cacheComponents` is partial in vinext: `"use cache"` pages render and reuse
  results in memory, but no CDN or data cache adapter is configured, so pages
  answer `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
- `next/image` is served unoptimized.
- The 4 external rewrites to infrastructure and calendar forward credential
  headers, matching Next.js.


## Production migration deployment proof

The Production Deployment Planner calls `web-cloudflare-production.yaml`
for each admitted `production` revision. The job uses the Cloudflare Workers
API to read the gateway and every activated vinext family's serving version.
The gateway flags and service bindings must match the committed vinext
inventory. Each Worker must serve one version at 100%, and the job rechecks
the serving versions before recording success. The version upload message
identifies the build commit. For vinext it must agree with the build stamp
binding. A 12-character stamp also needs an authenticated GitHub commit
resolution. [Cloudflare Worker versions and deployments](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/versions-and-deployments/)

Web families publish from `main`. During that arrangement the release gate
accepts the production commit itself, a descendant contained in `main`, or
an ancestor whose Worker build inputs are unchanged through the production
commit. GitHub's repository comparison proves the relationship, and
`verify-cloudflare-web-production.mjs` defines the build paths for each Worker
type. Diverged commits, incomplete comparisons, stale build inputs, mixed
traffic, and unknown routing withhold the marker. The job retries at two-minute
intervals for up to 20 minutes. A public build-info response can support a smoke
test.

The job records `cloudflare-production-web` with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, binding the
marker to the exact production SHA and planner attempt. The database workflow
checks the pinned caller, reusable workflow, verifier and recorder blobs,
the successful marker step, and the existing successful staging marker.
Manual recovery requires the same Web proof. A missing marker keeps migration
apply closed. Check the producer's Worker/version summary, coordinate an
authorized Web publication with the serving owner, then rerun the planner on
the pinned production SHA.

### Move vinext publication to the production branch

1. With the Web owner, qualify the active family build matrix and gateway
   configuration from one pinned `production` SHA on CI. Stamp each upload
   with its full build SHA. Retain the current serving Worker version IDs and
   gateway routing preimage.
2. Stage the version set and verify representative route families and gateway
   bindings before assigning traffic. Serialize the production publisher with
   the serving owner, and fence activation against a moved production ref or
   newer deployment. Keep one-step rollback to the retained version set.
3. After staged and production qualification, make the planner's proof depend
   on that publication, require exact SHA equality for all serving Workers,
   and review the resulting producer contract pins. Verify an exact-SHA
   marker and separate staging proof before authorizing a database apply.
